newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU nations urged not to send ambassadors to Iran.
newsitem.headline: EU nations urged not to send ambassadors to Iran.

text.p: The Netherlands urged EU partners on Wednesday not to send ambassadors back to Tehran, after Iran ruled out the return of German and Danish envoys over a German court ruling that Iranian leaders ordered killings in Berlin.
The Hague, which presently holds the EU's rotating presidency, said Iranian diplomats would be summoned to explain their country's latest move.

"The Presidency will make it clear to the Iranian charge d'affaires that the EU policy with regard to Iran is supported by all EU member states and the EU will not accept that Iran takes arbitrary measures against some member states for a policy supported by all," the Dutch government said.
The EU decided on Tuesday to suspend political dialogue with Tehran following a German court ruling that Iran's leaders ordered the 1992 assassination of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.

All EU nations, with the exception of Greece, withdrew their ambassadors from Tehran for consultations following the April 10 German court ruling, and the angry reaction it provoked from Iran's authorities.
EU foreign ministers meeting in Luxembourg agreed, however, its members should be free to send their ambassadors back to Iran if they wanted.

Iran said on Wednesday that a quick return of Germany's ambassador would not be welcomed and it may even be pleased if he never returned. The return of Denmark's ambassador was also reportedly blocked.
The EU's decision to allow its ambassadors to return has been heavily criticised by Germany's opposition parties.
